{
  "segment_function": "argument",
  "claims": [
    {
      "claim": "The crucial difference between indoor and outdoor spaces is that indoors can be designed comprehensively as a whole to facilitate or discourage specific patterns, whereas the lack of full enclosure in outdoor spaces makes it more challenging to impose a totalizing form upon them.",
      "claim_type": "author_position",
      "supporting_excerpt": "The crucial difference is simply that the indoors lends itself to being designed comprehensively , as some kind of whole, with an eye toward facilitating certain patterns of use, movement, and encounter and discouraging others;\nand while outdoor spaces have also been subject to the same sort of design,\nsometimes in a highly rationalizing and regimented spirit, the fact that they\nare not fully enclosed makes it more challenging to impose a totalizing\nform upon them.",
      "support_kind": "direct",
      "confidence": 1.0
    },
    {
      "claim": "Being outdoors as a sensate creature exposes one through the senses to a wider field of possibilities for the unanticipated or peripheral summoning of attention because the outdoors is intransigently interstitial.",
      "claim_type": "author_position",
      "supporting_excerpt": "What\nmatters about the outdoors, from this perspective, is that it is intransigently\ninterstitial; and to be outdoors, as a sensate creature, is to be exposed\nthrough the senses to a wider ﬁeld of possibilities for the unanticipated —\nwe might say , peripheral— summoning of one ’s attention.",
      "support_kind": "direct",
      "confidence": 1.0
    }
  ],
